                   SOUTHWESTERN ELECTRIC POWER COMPANY’S
             SECOND PETITION FOR REVIEW AND MOTION TO CONSOLIDATE

         Southwestern Electric Power Company (SWEPCO) files this petition appealing the rate

decisions adopted by the cities of Atlanta, Bloomburg, Center, Clarksville City, Gladewater, Grand

Saline, Hallsville, Hughes Springs, Kilgore, Longview, Marshall, Memphis, Mount Pleasant,

Mount Vernon, Overton, Pittsburg, Queen City, Wake Village, Waskom, Winnsboro, and

Winona. 1 SWEPCO also appeals the failure to timely act on SWEPCO’s tariff proposal, as

described below. This appeal is filed pursuant to § 33.051 of the Public Utility Regulatory Act

(PURA). In support of this appeal and motion, SWEPCO would show the following:

                                I.    SWEPCO’s Requested Tariff Approval

         On October 3, 2025, SWEPCO filed with the Public Utility Commission of Texas

(Commission) an application for authority to amend its tariffs for retail service to include a new

standard form contract for Electric Service – Large Load (ES-LL Contract) customers. On

December 29, 2026, SWEPCO filed its request that its proposed new ES-LL Contract be effective

35 days from that filing, consistent with 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 22.33(c). Concurrent with that


         1
           SWEPCO appealed the inaction of the cities of Bloomburg, Grand Saline, Hallsville, Hughes Springs,
Memphis, Mount Vernon, Overton, Queen City, and Wake Village on February 19, 2026; however, SWEPCO
received copies of these city’s resolutions denying SWEPCO’s proposal to amend its tariffs for retail service to include
a new standard form contract for Electric Service – Large Load from CARD counsel on February 25. Out of an
abundance of caution, SWEPCO is appealing these resolutions at this time to ensure the ability for SWEPCO to
achieve system wide rates.

 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-07507
 PUC Docket No. 58796

 filing, SWEPCO provided notice of the application amendment to all municipalities in its service

territory that retain exclusive jurisdiction over SWEPCO’s rates and tariffs.

         In the resolutions identified in the table below, the following cities adopted resolutions that

denied SWEPCO’s requested rate change and kept SWEPCO’s existing rates in effect:

Each of the ordinances/resolutions from the above municipalities included a provision that a copy

of the ordinance/resolution was to be served on SWEPCO. However, SWEPCO was only served

via electronic mail on February 24 and 25, 2026. Therefore, this appeal is filed within thirty (30)

days of the date that SWEPCO received notice of the municipal decisions. A copy of each

ordinance/resolution is attached as Exhibit 1.

          Additionally, SWEPCO appeals the rate decisions of those cities that have retained original

jurisdiction over its rates, operations, and services and that have failed to timely act on SWEPCO’s

rate request. In its rate request filed with these cities, SWEPCO indicated that the effective date

of its rate request was 35 days after the filing of the petition and statement of intent and requested

such date be extended by the cities to the maximum extent allowed by PURA § 36.108(a)(1) —

90 days from the date the requested rate would otherwise become effective. Many cities failed to

act and through that inaction, effectively denied the requested suspension and approved the

requested rate relief. 2 This appeal of these cities’ failure to act is necessary to preserve coordinated

system-wide rates throughout SWEPCO’s retail service territory. The Commission and Texas

courts have recognized the value of providing and maintaining system-wide rates. 3

         This appeal is filed pursuant to PURA § 33.051, which allows a party to a municipal

proceeding, such as SWEPCO, to appeal to the Commission a “decision” of the municipal

governing body. A decision not to act on a rate request may be appealed to the Commission.

Otherwise, the Commission is robbed of its exclusive appellate jurisdiction granted by PURA




         2
             PURA § 36.108(c).
         3
           City of Allen v. Public Util. Comm’n, 161 S.W.3d 195, 207 (Tex. App.—Austin 2005, no pet.) (noting, “the
contemporary reality that the assets of an integrated utility simultaneously serve all its customers rendering the
allocation of cost on a territorial basis an inappropriate method of rate-setting in the context of present-day
technology”) (quoting City of Corpus Christi v. Public Util. Comm’n, 572 S.W.2d 290, 296 (Tex. 1978)); see also
Rulemaking Related to Periodic Rate Adjustments, Project No. 39465, Order at 53 (September 27, 2011) (“The
commission agrees with Electric Utilities and REP Coalition that the rule should make an electric utility’s appeal
automatic; doing so avoids the cost of actually appealing the city action or inaction and ensures that the appeal is
made. Because an appeal is necessary to ensure a system-wide DCRF, making the appeal automatic helps ensure a
system-wide DCRF.”); Tex. Util. Code § 33.055(a) (An interim rate order may be issued “to effect uniform system-
wide rates.”); Application of Lower Colorado River Auth., 12 Tex. P.U.C. Bull. 1856 (Tex. P.U.C. May 13, 1987)
(Uniform rates must be applied system-wide and not be based upon the locality of the utility’s service area at which a
customer is served).

 § 32.001(b). Further, appeal upon a city’s failure or refusal to act on an application within a

specified period is necessary to preserve parties’ appellate rights. 4

         The municipalities that have failed to act by denying SWEPCO’s request or timely

suspending rates include: Daingerfield, Hawkins, Henderson, Mineola, Mount Enterprise, Naples,

New London, Wellington, and White Oak. SWEPCO believes that a number of these cities may

have previously taken action on SWEPCO’s proposed new ES-LL Contract; however, SWEPCO

has not yet received a copy of any ordinances/resolutions. Accordingly, out of an abundance of

caution, SWEPCO is now appealing the inaction. If SWEPCO receives an ordinance from these

municipalities, SWEPCO will appeal those decisions in a future filing.

                                               III.      Jurisdiction

         The Commission has jurisdiction over this appeal in accordance with PURA §§ 32.001(b),

33.051, and 33.053.

                                         IV.      Motion to Consolidate

         SWEPCO requests that its appeal of the ordinances/resolutions of the cities of Atlanta,

Bloomburg, Center, Clarksville City, Gladewater, Grand Saline, Hallsville, Hughes Springs,

Kilgore, Longview, Marshall, Memphis, Mount Pleasant, Mount Vernon, Overton, Pittsburg,

Queen City, Wake Village, Waskom, Winnsboro, and Winona be consolidated with Docket

No. 58796. Additionally, SWEPCO requests that its appeals of the failure to act by the cities of

Daingerfield, Hawkins, Henderson, Mineola, Mount Enterprise, Naples, New London,

Wellington, and White Oak also be consolidated with Docket No. 58796. SWEPCO’s appeal

            Cf. City of Sherman v. Railroad Comm’n of Tex., 454 S.W.2d 762, 764 (Tex. Civ. App.—Austin 1970, no
writ) (An appeal may be taken upon rejection by the municipal government of an application for a rate increase or its
failure or refusal to act on the application within a specified period. “The doctrine of primary jurisdiction assures the
agency, such as the Railroad Commission in this case, that it will not be bypassed on matters committed to it by law.”).

 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-07507

 involves issues of law and fact common to those involved in Docket No. 58796, and a separate

hearing of this appeal and Docket No. 58796 would result in unwarranted expenses, delay, or

substantial injustice.

                                         V.      Conclusion

         SWEPCO respectfully requests the Administrative Law Judge enter an order consolidating

this appeal with Docket No. 58796. SWEPCO further respectfully requests that upon final hearing,

SWEPCO be granted the rate relief requested in its petition and statement of intent. SWEPCO

further requests any further relief to which it may be justly entitled.
